article.title: GTA 6 nặng đến mức PS5 Pro cũng khó đạt 60 FPS
article.summary: Thông tin này xuất hiện sau buổi trải nghiệm GTA 6 kéo dài khoảng ba giờ tại Rockstar North của YouTuber Davy Jones. Trong đó, Giám đốc phát triển Rob Nelson đã trực tiếp chơi game hơn hai giờ.
article.dek: Thông tin này xuất hiện sau buổi trải nghiệm GTA 6 kéo dài khoảng ba giờ tại Rockstar North của YouTuber Davy Jones.
article.hook: Thông tin này xuất hiện sau buổi trải nghiệm GTA 6 kéo dài khoảng ba giờ tại Rockstar North của YouTuber Davy Jones.

sections.heading: Bối cảnh: điều gì đang đổi
sections.body: Thông tin này xuất hiện sau buổi trải nghiệm GTA 6 kéo dài khoảng ba giờ tại Rockstar North của YouTuber Davy Jones. Trong đó, Giám đốc phát triển Rob Nelson đã trực tiếp chơi game hơn hai giờ. Jones cho biết trò chơi chạy ở 30 FPS trong suốt phần trình diễn.

sections.heading: Các nguồn đang khớp nhau ở đâu
sections.body: GTA 6 xây dựng thế giới mở đông đúc với nhiều hệ thống mô phỏng, tạo áp lực xử lý lớn lên phần cứng của hệ máy console.

sections.heading: Tác động thực tế với người đọc
sections.body: Khi được hỏi liệu GTA 6 có chế độ ưu tiên hiệu năng hay không, Nelson cho biết trò chơi hiện chạy ở 30 FPS và ông cần trao đổi với đội ngũ kỹ thuật để biết khả năng đạt 60 FPS khi phát hành hoặc sau đó. Rockstar vì thế chưa đưa ra bất kỳ cam kết nào về chế độ 60 FPS trên console.

sections.heading: Ai nên chú ý lúc này
sections.body: Mức 30 FPS vốn không xa lạ với game của Rockstar. GTA 5 từng giới hạn ở 30 FPS trên PS3 và PS4 trước khi phiên bản dành cho PS5 bổ sung tùy chọn 60 FPS. Tuy nhiên, GTA 6 có thể là bài toán khác khi lượng công việc mà hệ thống phải xử lý không chỉ tập trung vào chất lượng đồ họa.

sections.heading: Điều cần theo dõi tiếp
sections.body: CPU có thể là một trong những giới hạn khiến GTA 6 khó đạt tốc độ khung hình cao. Một thế giới đông NPC cùng các hệ thống giao thông, vật lý, thời tiết và AI hoạt động liên tục tạo ra lượng tính toán lớn mà CPU phải đảm nhiệm.

draft_context.description: Những thông tin mới nhất về hiệu năng GTA 6 phần nào cho thấy sức nặng của thế giới mà Rockstar đang xây dựng.
paragraphs: Thông tin này xuất hiện sau buổi trải nghiệm GTA 6 kéo dài khoảng ba giờ tại Rockstar North của YouTuber Davy Jones. Trong đó, Giám đốc phát triển Rob Nelson đã trực tiếp chơi game hơn hai giờ. Jones cho biết trò chơi chạy ở 30 FPS trong suốt phần trình diễn.
GTA 6 xây dựng thế giới mở đông đúc với nhiều hệ thống mô phỏng, tạo áp lực xử lý lớn lên phần cứng của hệ máy console

Mức 30 FPS vốn không xa lạ với game của Rockstar. GTA 5 từng giới hạn ở 30 FPS trên PS3 và PS4 trước khi phiên bản dành cho PS5 bổ sung tùy chọn 60 FPS. Tuy nhiên, GTA 6 có thể là bài toán khác khi lượng công việc mà hệ thống phải xử lý không chỉ tập trung vào chất lượng đồ họa.

CPU có thể là một trong những giới hạn khiến GTA 6 khó đạt tốc độ khung hình cao. Một thế giới đông NPC cùng các hệ thống giao thông, vật lý, thời tiết và AI hoạt động liên tục tạo ra lượng tính toán lớn mà CPU phải đảm nhiệm.

Điều này đặc biệt quan trọng với PS5 Pro . Mẫu console này có GPU mạnh hơn PS5 tiêu chuẩn và được trang bị công nghệ nâng cấp hình ảnh PSSR 2, nhưng CPU không có bước nhảy tương ứng về hiệu năng. Nếu GTA 6 thực sự bị giới hạn bởi CPU, sức mạnh xử lý đồ họa bổ sung khó tự nó đưa trò chơi từ 30 lên 60 FPS.

Tim Cook sẽ tiếp tục làm việc tại Apple với vai trò Chủ tịch điều hành và hỗ trợ công ty trong một số lĩnh vực, trong đó có làm việc với các nhà hoạch định chính sách trên toàn thế giới, theo thông báo của hãng “Táo khuyết”. Ông cũng đóng vai trò quan trọng trong việc đưa doanh thu mảng Dịch vụ của Apple vượt mốc 100 tỷ USD, trở thành mảng kinh doanh lớn thứ hai của công ty, chỉ sau iPhone. (Ảnh: Mạnh Hùng) Steve Jobs tuyển Tim Cook vào Apple năm 1998 và bổ nhiệm ông làm Phó Chủ tịch điều hành phụ trách bán hàng toàn cầu năm 2002, trước khi đưa ông lên vị trí Giám đốc vận hành (COO) vào năm 2005. Năm 2011, Tim Cook kế nhiệm Steve Jobs và trở thành CEO Apple. Trong thời gian lãnh đạo, vị CEO này tận dụng kinh nghiệm về chuỗi cung ứng để mở rộng đáng kể hoạt động kinh doanh của Apple. Vốn hóa thị trường của công ty tăng từ khoảng 350 tỷ USD lên hơn 4.000 tỷ USD, tương đương mức tăng khoảng 1.000%. Một dấu ấn quan trọng khác của Tim Cook là thúc đẩy Apple chuyển từ chip Intel sang chip do hãng tự thiết kế cho dòng máy Mac. Việc tự phát triển chip giúp cải thiện đáng kể hiệu năng máy tính, đồng thời mang lại thời lượng pin vượt trội, lợi thế mà các đối thủ chỉ mới bắt kịp trong những năm gần đây. John Ternus tiếp quản vị trí CEO Apple trong bối cảnh công ty đang bước vào giai đoạn chuyển đổi lớn. Apple đang nỗ lực cải thiện năng lực trí tuệ nhân tạo (AI) sau khi được cho là chậm chân hơn các đối thủ như Microsoft và Google. John Ternus và Tim Cook tại Apple Park. (Ảnh: Apple) Apple được kỳ vọng ra mắt phiên bản Siri mới sử dụng các mô hình AI Gemini của Google tại Hội nghị các nhà phát triển toàn cầu (WWDC) vào tháng 6. Bên cạnh đó, Apple được cho là đang chuẩn bị một trong những thay đổi lớn nhất đối với iPhone, với mẫu iPhone màn hình gập dự kiến ra mắt không lâu sau khi Tim Cook rời ghế CEO. Apple chuẩn bị sự kiện iPhone khác lạ nhất trong nhiều năm VOV.VN - Apple đã chốt ngày ra mắt iPhone mới, nhưng kế hoạch được cho là sẽ phá vỡ truyền thống giới thiệu toàn bộ dòng máy.

article.summary: Hosting software vendor tells customers to reset credentials and hunt for malicious packages. draft_context.source_title: 33-hour BGP hijack of Softaculous traffic prompts security scramble
draft_context.description: Softaculous and Virtualizor customers are being urged to reset credentials and inspect their servers after a 33-hour BGP hijacking incident diverted traffic and delivered malware to a handful of installations. Softaculous makes software for the web hosting industry, while its Virtualizor control panel is used by providers and administrators to deploy and manage virtual private servers. Beginning at around 20:57 UTC on August 28, an unrelated network began announcing a block of Hetzner IP addresses used by Softaculous, diverting some traffic intended for the vendor's systems to an attacker-controlled server. German hosting provider Hetzner is one of Softaculous's upstream infrastructure providers. The affected addresses served "a number of Softaculous systems," including Virtualizor's software update endpoint and Softaculous's client and billing site. The attacker pulled off the BGP hijack by announcing a more specific IP address range than Hetzner normally advertised. Under standard BGP route selection, the more specific route took precedence wherever it was accepted. According to Softaculous, the attacker was also able to secure a valid TLS certificate from Let's Encrypt because the certificate authority's automated domain-ownership validation was routed through the hijack too. This allowed affected connections to reach the attacker's server without triggering the certificate warnings that might otherwise have alerted users. According to the vendor's timeline, the unauthorized route was initially "accepted by essentially every internet vantage point that receives it," although it flapped repeatedly rather than remaining continuously available. Softaculous said it reported the issues to Hetzner at around 08:50 UTC on August 29. The hosting provider began directly announcing the same, more-specific address range, cutting the observed diversion to almost zero for roughly 11 hours. The unauthorized announcement returned at around 20:00 UTC and was again widely accepted, beginning a second wave that lasted roughly ten hours. The route was withdrawn between 05:50 and 06:10 UTC on August 30, after which normal routing was restored globally. While either wave was active, Softaculous estimates that a given server had roughly a 72 percent chance of being on a network that routed the affected address range through the attacker. The figure is based on the proportion of RIPE routing collector peers carrying the hijacked route, not the volume of traffic intercepted, the vendor said. Anyone who logged into the Softaculous client area during the incident window is advised to reset that password immediately, as well as anywhere else it was reused. Customers who entered card details during the same window should also review their statements. Softaculous said it does not process cards on its own servers and instead uses payment gateways, but an affected session may have been diverted before reaching them. More seriously, the vendor confirmed that a malicious Virtualizor update package was delivered to a handful of installations whose update checks passed through the attacker's server. "Our product update clients did not yet cryptographically verify update packages, so a modified package would not have been rejected on that basis." Because those downloads never reached its own logs, Softaculous said it "cannot produce a definitive list" of affected installations. It is therefore telling every Virtualizor operator to treat their server as in scope for checks – not necessarily as compromised. Softaculous did not describe the malware's capabilities, but identified a systemd unit at /etc/systemd/system/java-jre-update.service as an indicator of compromise. Operators that find it are advised not to delete it immediately, but to contact the vendor so evidence can be preserved. The vendor has not identified malicious packages targeting Backuply, Softaculous, SitePad, Webuzo, or its other products, although its investigation continues. Virtualizor operators should rotate and restrict their API credentials, check for unknown SSH keys and accounts, inspect scheduled tasks and outbound connections, and regenerate client-area API keys. Softaculous is also invalidating client-area sessions created during the incident window. Softaculous did not disclose how many customers downloaded the malicious update or may have handed credentials to the attacker. It said only that the confirmed infections amounted to "a handful of servers rather than the general Virtualizor user base." ®

sections.heading: Context: what is changing
sections.body: 0 • Lanh Nguyen / Android Authority co/AAGooglePreferredSource"> Add us as preferred source TL;DR Samsung is expanding the One UI 9 beta program to additional Galaxy phones. The Galaxy Z Fold 7 and Galaxy Z Flip 7 have been confirmed as eligible. The program will be available in India, Korea, the UK, and the US.

sections.heading: Where the sources line up
sections.body: While stable One UI 9 is available on the Galaxy Z Fold 8 series and Flip 8, Samsung still isn’t quite ready to release the stable version to its older Galaxy phones. The tech giant just rolled out the eighth beta for the Galaxy S26 series . However, the company is at least letting its other phones get a taste of the next major update.

sections.heading: Practical impact for readers
sections.body: Earlier today, South Korea, the UK, and India began receiving the first One UI 9 beta update for the Galaxy S25 series . draft_context.source_title: I tried Sony's new ULT Tower party speakers, and they shook me to my core — here's everything you need to know about the striking new models
draft_context.description: Sony reveals 3 new party speakers: ULT Tower 5, ULT Tower 7, and ULT Tower Max ULT Tower 3, £349 (around $470 / AU$660); ULT Tower 7, £499, (approx. $680 / AU$940); ULT Max £1,299 (about $1,800 / AU$2,500) New circular woofers, multiple sound modes, 360-degree party sound Sony has revealed three new party speakers and — hurrah! — I’ve had the chance to hear them for myself. The Sony ULT Tower 5, ULT Tower 7, and ULT Tower Max look to offer almighty audio output for parties, DJ sets, or even karaoke sessions, with various ways to play and connect. These bass-conscious new speakers are built around newly developed large, circular woofers (a departure from Sony's almost rectangular X-Balanced woofer unit, typically seen across the ULT range), and according to Sony, the Max model specifically delivers the most powerful bass in the ULT Power series to date. Their bold designs — which also deviate a fair bit from previous ULT speakers — as well as their massive power outputs and broad connectivity options could make them a major rival for the likes of JBL’s PartyBox models, if the sound is right. Just how good do Sony’s new ULT speakers sound? I attended an impressive demo and I’ll reveal what I thought shortly. First, let’s run through everything I learned about Sony’s Towers, from technical specifications to nifty new features. Taking a closer look (Image credit: Sony) Let’s look closer at each of the three new ULT Tower speakers, and go through the key technical details. The ULT Tower 5 is the smallest in the new line-up, but it still packs quite the punch. It contains a 230mm woofer and two tweeters with a 300W maximum power output. Meanwhile, the ULT Tower 7 boasts a larger 280mm woofer, alongside two mid-range units, and four tweeters — two front-facing, and two rear-facing. The rear tweeters are also angled for a wider soundstage. The ULT Tower 7 has a 420W maximum power output. Finally, the ULT Tower Max is a true beast of a speaker. It has three woofers, two front-facing, one rear-facing. But it also comes with two-midrange units, and four tweeters, two of which are rear-facing. Its high-power amplifier delivers 2,150W of output, making it one of the most powerful party speakers I’ve ever encountered. I want to focus in on the woofers for a moment, because Sony were really keen to stress the changes made for the new ULT Tower models. Unlike some previous models, the new Towers have circular driver units for the woofers, rather than the ‘X-Balanced’ alternative. Sony Product Manager Mike Somerset told me: “X-Balanced is fantastic for a smaller, compact system and maximizing the surface area inside — let’s say, for a rectangular speaker unit, you know. And it also delivers a really great, impressive ‘attack’ bass. But with these, we really wanted to emphasize deep bass — and to be able to do that we’ve moved to this circular driver unit”. The speakers also have large capacity cabinets and ULT Duct tech, which is intended to help each model produce “deeper, more powerful bass with greater authority”. Do it your way (Image credit: Sony) As well as talking up the outrageous power of the ULT Towers, Sony was keen to share the impressive customizability of the speakers. That’s because there are a number of sound modes, all of which are designed for specific situations and genres. There are two ULT modes. The first, Sony says, is intended to enhance deep bass for “a rich, low frequency sound that makes your heart tremble,” with the second made to ramp things up even further for “even greater power, delivering body-shaking bass and strong sound pressure”. What’s perhaps more interesting, though, are the ‘Flat’ and ‘Live’ options. As you’d expect, Flat is designed to make a track sound as it was intended to at the mixing desk, with a more neutral, balanced approach. Live, however, is focused on delivering a more spacious sound, with a strong emphasis on vocal clarity. The speakers were tuned with the help of a number of "Hip-Hop sound creators," including producer, songwriter, and DJ, Dready, who spoke with me about the EQ adjustment process. On the Flat tuning, he said, “That’s how I would have it on a DJ set, because obviously on the controller you have the lows, mids, and highs, and we just gave it a nice blend… so, you know, when people take it, they can express themselves how they want”. Of course, if you want to personalize things even further, you can connect to the speaker with the Sony Sound Connect app and make use of the multi-band custom equalizer instead. So…how good do they sound? (Image credit: Sony) Do the ULT Tower speakers sound any good? Allow me to go through them one by one. The ULT Tower 5 arguably impressed me the most, relative to its size and cost. Sure, it leaves out the 360-degree Party Sound feature that the larger models adopt (presumably due to its lack of rear-facing drivers), but its raw power and regimented sound were hard to ignore. When listening to Luther by Kendrick Lamar and SZA, the speaker showed its considerable versatility. The vocal sample in the intro sounded textured and resonant, but then the drive and power of deep bass hit with surprising impact. Bass, though the clear star of the show, sounded controlled yet powerful, and never shrouded vocals in the mids or drums up high. We cycled between the various sound modes, and the switch between an ‘attack’ bass and deep bass mode was pretty striking. It was incredibly seamless to sift through the different modes using the ULT logo — which also happens to be a button. It’s too early to say if it’s a sure-fire hit, but for £349 (around $470 / AU$660, but these are guesstimates based on the UK pricing right now, since Sony hasn't disclosed official pricing for these regions at the time of writing), the ULT Tower 5 sounded far more impressive than some rivals I’ve tested in its price and size class. Things got even louder when we switched to the ULT Tower 7. We tried listening to Don’t Start Now by Dua Lipa, and low-frequency sounds were full-bodied, agile, and striking. Treble sounded pretty forward to me, with higher-pitched percussion seeming highly prominent, while vocals sounded clear and well-weighted in the mix. We also tried out Money by Pink Floyd, which is a great testing track for any speaker. The 360-degree sound seemed pretty effective here, and when pairing two ULT Tower 7s together in stereo mode, the spaciousness of the track was brilliantly recreated. Vocals and guitars sounded tonally accurate and well-separated, but that low-end still came through with immense drive. Finally, we hopped over to try out the behemoth that is the Sony ULT Tower Max. I’m no stranger to a rave, and the Max made me feel like I was listening to a set at my local venue. I was able to pick a track of my choosing, so I threw on Breather by Chris Stassy. And this perfectly showed off the huge sound of the ULT Tower Max. The pumping, deep bass was genuinely earth-shaking, and I could almost feel it vibrating through my soul. But spacey sounds in the mid-range still came through cleanly, and were provided plenty of room to express themselves. If you want truly mesmerizing power at a relatively moderate cost (all things considered), then the ULT Tower Max could be one to keep an eye on. We also tried pairing ten of the ULT models together, and… as you can probably imagine, the results were palpable. Auracast technology allows multiple models to chain together, and even the LED lighting syncs up across each speaker, making for an especially immersive listening experience. Final thoughts: enticing new designs and competitive pricing (Image credit: Sony) The new ULT Towers feel like Sony’s attempt to genuinely take on JBL in the party speaker arena, with the latter being particularly dominant in this field. The party speaker segment has increased in popularity as of late, and we’ve even seen new entrants like Marshall releasing its Bromley 450 and Bromley 750 speakers. But could the ULT Towers rival the likes of JBL’s Partybox models? Well, at a glance, I think they could. They offer incredible power, more than a lot of mainstream competitors, they have a new design with attractive lighting, refined sound with rounded woofers, and plenty of ways to make them sound right for you. And that’s not to mention the wide connectivity options, including Bluetooth, RCA, XLR, and USB-C. For the power and features on offer, they’re also priced relatively modestly, with the Tower 5 coming in at £349 (around $470 / AU$660), the Tower 7 at £499 (in the region of $680 / AU$940), and the ULT Max at £1,299 (about $1,800 / AU$2,500). I was also impressed to see the battery life of the speakers, with 30 hours on the ULT Tower 7 and 20 hours on the Tower 5 — that’s quite a lot of playtime given the power demands. And although features such as 360-degree audio and sound modes are exciting, Sound Field Optimization (which analyzes speaker placement and surround noise levels to offer the best sound possible) are even better. That’s something that could really set this model apart. We’ll have to test the ULT Tower models out for a bit longer to determine whether they can compete with the best, but so far, it’s fair to say that they’ve impressed me. ]]>

article.summary: 30 years on, it's still alpha, but 0.4.16 brings plenty of bug fixes and quality-of-life improvements - just in time for Windows XP's 25th anniversary. draft_context.source_title: ReactOS 0.4.16 serves '90s Windows nostalgia with fewer bugs
draft_context.description: If you're pining away for the days when Windows ran well on 64 MB of RAM, there's a new version of open source NT clone ReactOS promising easier installation and fewer bugs. ReactOS 0.4.16 was announced over the weekend after a year and a half of development, and its list of improvements is substantial. For those unfamiliar with the ReactOS project, it’s a long-running effort (it spun up in 1996) to create an open source equivalent of Windows NT, with the aim of running Windows applications and drivers. If you miss the halcyon days of Windows XP that began a quarter of a century ago, in other words, it's the project for you. Given that it’s an open source project driven by a group of volunteers who’ve had to dodge accusations that they’re just ripping off old copies of a research kernel, compatibility, ease of installation, and stability have all been sore spots for ReactOS. A number of essential elements have been fixed and improved as of 0.4.16, per the team. “We’re excited to showcase the improvements we’ve made,” the ReactOS builders said in their release notes, with “a unified bootcd and livecd image; video, audio, networking, and storage stack improvements; a new installation type; and third-party code syncs” all mentioned as having been added. The unified bootcd and livecd mean a single disc can now be used to boot into a temporary version of ReactOS to have a poke around, and to install the OS itself. A graphical installer is also included in the new unified disk image, meaning that there’s no longer a need to navigate a truly old-fashioned interface to get up and running. Fixed OS functions Running old-fashioned software (or modern iterations of it) on newer hardware is bound to be a complicated mess, and that’s true for ReactOS. Video drivers from “all major … vendors” have been causing issues in the experimental OS for years, the team notes, but apparently one source of the problem has finally been identified and addressed in 0.4.16. The kernel’s system page table entries, it turns out, were filling up when loading third-party graphics drivers because they eat up more memory than most others, so the memory manager layout was modified to increase the number of system PTEs. A different problem with blank OpenGL windows on AMD video drivers was resolved separately. Both improvements “fixed many edge case bugs in our win32k.sys driver,” the ReactOS team noted. A new HD audio bus driver was brought in to replace an older implementation that was never quite finished, addressing frequent bugchecks when attempting to install HD audio controller drivers. As for storage, the 2009 implementation of UniATA gave ReactOS the ability to recognize disk partitions over 8 GB, but the aging driver has since begun to cause slow boot times and load failures. It’s been replaced with a new ATA driver that also allows ReactOS to boot in more environments, including first-generation Hyper-V VMs. A disk cleanup utility was also added. Networking support has also been improved, with support for more adapters and virtual environments added. Asynchronous connections are now supported as well. There’s also a new headless Server Core installation type of ReactOS available with this release that loads a full Win32 subsystem without the GUI, similar to Windows Server Core that Microsoft released with Windows Server 2008. Finally, the ReactOS team has abandoned Windows Server 2003 compatibility restrictions, meaning that its Wine fork designed to interface with Windows-like kernels is no longer limited to Wine 2.x and 3.x, the latest of which was released in 2018. The abandonment of that restriction means ReactOS has been able to update its Wine fork toward Wine 10.0, which was released in early 2025, with 0.4.16 incorporating a significant amount of that work. Support for WineVDM, which increases compatibility for 16-bit Windows applications, was also added in the release. “The mission for ReactOS is to ‘[Run] your favorite Windows applications and drivers in an open-source environment you can trust,’” the team said. “With each release we come closer to fulfilling this goal.” You can download version 0.4.16 of ReactOS here, but the team’s usual warning applies: Despite being a 30-year-old project, it is still in an alpha state “and provides no guarantee of stability, of safety for your files, or that it will work at all on your hardware.” ®

For those unfamiliar with the ReactOS project, it’s a long-running effort (it spun up in 1996) to create an open source equivalent of Windows NT, with the aim of running Windows applications and drivers.
If you miss the halcyon days of Windows XP that began a quarter of a century ago, in other words, it's the project for you.

Given that it’s an open source project driven by a group of volunteers who’ve had to dodge accusations that they’re just ripping off old copies of a research kernel, compatibility, ease of installation, and stability have all been sore spots for ReactOS. A number of essential elements have been fixed and improved as of 0.4.16, per the team.

“We’re excited to showcase the improvements we’ve made,” the ReactOS builders said in their release notes, with “a unified bootcd and livecd image; video, audio, networking, and storage stack improvements; a new installation type; and third-party code syncs” all mentioned as having been added.
